instructions: Up to 2 weeks ahead, or at least an hour before breakfast, heat the oven to 300°F with a rack in the middle. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment.
Roughly chop 1 1/4 cups of the pecans.
In a large bowl, stir together the 3 cups oats, 1 1/4 cups coconut flakes, the chopped pecans, 1/3 cup pumpkin seeds, 1 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp pumpkin pie spice and 1/2 tsp salt.
Pour in 1/2 cup maple syrup and the 1/3 cup oil. Stir until every oat looks shiny and there are no dry patches left at the bottom of the bowl.
Spread it over the baking sheet in an even layer and bake for 15 minutes.
Take the pan out and give it a stir with a spatula. Press it back into a flat, firm layer with the back of the spatula. That's what makes clusters.
Bake for another 15 to 20 minutes without stirring, until it's golden brown and smells toasty. Check it at 15 minutes. The edges brown first.
Scatter the 1 cup raisins over the hot pan. Leave it on the pan until it's completely cool, about 30 minutes. It turns crunchy as it cools.
Break it into clusters and keep it in a jar or an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 weeks.
To serve, divide the 3 cups yogurt between 4 bowls, about 3/4 cup each, and top each bowl with about 1/2 cup of the clusters.
advance_prep_notes: Bake the granola up to 2 weeks ahead, or at least an hour before breakfast, and keep it in a jar.
method_notes: All three bake oats, nuts and a sweetener coated in oil low and slow at 300°F on a lined sheet. Spend With Pennies (the lead) uses maple syrup and vegetable oil with coconut, nuts, seeds, cinnamon and pumpkin pie spice, and stirs raisins in once it comes out of the oven. Once Upon a Chef adds brown sugar and an egg white, stirs once at 15 minutes and then presses it flat for bigger clusters; Love and Lemons uses coconut oil and almond butter and presses it into a thick slab. This one follows the lead's ratios with Once Upon a Chef's stir and press. One batch makes about 7 cups, so after 4 bowls there's enough left for the rest of the week.
